history.hpi: Mother reports daughter has had a cold for two days and woke up this morning coughing and wheezing. Symptoms worsened over the last hour despite two puffs of her rescue inhaler at home. Known history of asthma with a prior ED visit and one hospital admission last year. No fever reported.
pastMedical: One prior hospital admission for asthma exacerbation
history.events: Mother called 911 after home rescue inhaler failed to relieve worsening wheeze and breathing effort

scene.location: Single-family home, living room, child sitting upright on mother's lap
scene.bystanders: Mother present, anxious, holding child upright; two older siblings in another room
visualCues: Child sitting upright, leaning slightly forward
Audible expiratory wheeze from across the room
Home nebulizer and empty albuterol MDI on coffee table
Child appears tired, minimal interest in surroundings

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 4-year-old female sitting upright on her mother's lap with audible expiratory wheezing, visible retractions, and a prolonged expiratory phase. She is tiring and speaking only in short phrases.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Labored, prolonged expiratory phase, intercostal/subcostal retractions, RR 44
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, rapid, skin pale and slightly diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, clings to mother
otherFindings: Diffuse expiratory wheezing bilaterally, decreased air movement at bases
Speaking only 2-3 words at a time

expectedActions.shortAction: Titrate supplemental O2 to target 94-98% SpO2
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Give supplemental oxygen for dyspnea to a target of 94–98% saturation. Escalate from a nasal cannula as needed to reach this goal
expectedActions.rationale: Corrects hypoxia while avoiding unnecessary hyperoxia.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Albuterol 5 mg nebulized with ipratropium 0.5 mg; repeat albuterol as needed
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Albuterol 5 mg nebulized (or 6 puffs metered dose inhaler) should be administered to all patients in respiratory distress with signs of bronchospasm (e.g., known asthmatics, quiet wheezers). Repeat at this dose with unlimited frequency for ongoing respiratory distress. Ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized should be given up to 3 doses in conjunction with albuterol
expectedActions.rationale: First-line bronchodilator therapy for bronchospasm; fixed dose per protocol regardless of age.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply continuous pulse oximetry and reassess work of breathing after each treatment
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Pulse oximetry and EtCO2 should be routinely used as adjuncts to other forms of monitoring in patients with respiratory complaints
expectedActions.rationale: Tracks response to treatment and identifies need for escalation.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes signs of bronchospasm in respiratory distress and administers weight-appropriate supplemental O2 along with nebulized albuterol/ipratropium per protocol.
Crew repeats nebulizer treatments without recognizing the lack of improvement, delaying escalation to IM epinephrine while the patient tires further.

phases.name: Duoneb and O2 started
phases.description: Crew applies supplemental oxygen titrated to a 94-98% target and administers a combined albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer treatment. Wheezing and effort persist despite the first treatment, with signs of distress continuing.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing bronchospasm in a distressed pediatric asthma patient, the crew provides O2 and starts nebulized albuterol/ipratropium, but the patient continues to show signs of significant distress after treatment.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Labored, RR 40, continued retractions, nebulizer mask in place
otherFindings: Wheezing persists diffusely despite nebulizer treatment
No clinical improvement after first nebulizer dose
Known asthmatic with prior hospitalization — high-risk features present

expectedActions.shortAction: Epinephrine 0.16 mg IM (16 kg × 0.01 mg/kg; max 0.3 mg), 1 mg/mL concentration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Epinephrine (0.01 mg/kg of 1 mg/mL solution IM, maximum dose of 0.3 mg) should only be administered for impending respiratory failure as adjunctive therapy when there are no clinical signs of improvement with the above treatments
expectedActions.rationale: Reserved for patients failing first-line bronchodilator therapy; adjunctive, not a replacement for nebulizers.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess work of breathing, SpO2, and EtCO2 waveform after epinephrine
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitoring: Pulse oximetry and EtCO2 should be routinely used as adjuncts to other forms of monitoring in patients with respiratory complaints
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms response to adjunctive therapy and guides further treatment.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.if: IM epi given for no improvement
transitions.condition: Despite nebulized bronchodilator therapy, the patient shows no clinical signs of improvement, prompting administration of IM epinephrine as adjunctive therapy.

phases.name: IM epi given for no improvement
phases.description: With no clinical improvement after nebulizer therapy and continued signs of significant distress, the crew administers weight-based IM epinephrine as adjunctive therapy.
phases.triggerCondition: The patient continues to show signs of distress (persistent wheeze, retractions, tachypnea) despite nebulized bronchodilators, meeting criteria for adjunctive IM epinephrine.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Improving, RR 34, decreased retractions within minutes of epi

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue O2, reassess vitals serially en route, transport to pediatric-capable facility
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring may be indicated in patients with respiratory distress associated with suspected acute or decompensated congestive heart failure (CHF) or dysrhythmia
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment detects early relapse of bronchospasm during transport.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: Work of breathing, SpO2, and air movement improve following epinephrine; patient is packaged for transport with continued monitoring.

phases.name: Improved and prepared for transport
phases.description: The patient's work of breathing has improved with decreased wheezing and retractions. She is repositioned for comfort and transported with continuous reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: Following IM epinephrine and continued nebulizer therapy, the patient shows sustained clinical improvement and is prepared for transport.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, playing with stuffed animal
otherFindings: Mild expiratory wheeze remaining, much improved air movement

phases.name: Escalation to epi delayed
phases.description: The crew repeats nebulizer treatments without recognizing the persistent lack of improvement. The patient tires further, with worsening retractions and a falling respiratory rate despite ongoing wheeze — a concerning sign of impending respiratory failure.
phases.triggerCondition: Nebulizer therapy is repeated without escalating to IM epinephrine despite ongoing signs of significant distress; the patient begins to fatigue.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but tiring, wheeze becoming quieter
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Severely labored, RR falling to 18 despite distress — ominous sign
otherFindings: Wheeze quieting despite ongoing distress — decreasing air movement, not improvement
Falling respiratory rate is a sign of impending respiratory failure, not improvement

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize impending respiratory failure; give IM epinephrine 0.16 mg IM immediately, prepare for BVM support
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The following signs are concerning for impending respiratory failure and require immediate intervention. Epinephrine (0.01 mg/kg of 1 mg/mL solution IM, maximum dose of 0.3 mg) should only be administered for impending respiratory failure as adjunctive therapy when there are no clinical signs of improvement with the above treatments
expectedActions.rationale: A falling respiratory rate with worsening hypoxia in a fatiguing asthmatic signals impending arrest, not improvement.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)
